source.title: Towards Atoms of Large Language Models
source.authors: Chenhui Hu; Pengfei Cao; Yubo Chen; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own SAE reconstruction results under different activation designs, capacities, and data sources. It argues that standard ReLU SAEs fail to identify the proposed units while threshold-activated SAEs can reconstruct activations with high fidelity, refining claims about training-related limits on SAE reconstruction.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure linear predictability of SAE errors, per-token error norms or token overlap across SAE sizes, loss effects of replacing activations, or the functional consequences of retaining the error term. It does report reconstruction fidelity for SAEs with different training designs. Reported monosemanticity results and cited dark-matter findings are not rows for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own SAEs and reports reconstruction R2 under different conditions. 1−R2 is the unexplained share of the activation, so it measures the size of the SAE error. JumpReLU TSAEs reach about 99.9% R2 and ReLU SAEs about 91–97% on the same Gemma2-2B data. Corpus-trained GemmaScope/LlamaScope SAEs reach 48.8%. The paper argues explicitly that the SAE limit comes from missing threshold activation, not from the linear–nonlinear mechanism. This bears on V6 (dark matter as a training artifact) and on V2's claim that error does not vanish with scale. The setting is narrow: final-token activations of about 20K subject entities per layer.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also attribute standard SAE incompleteness ('dark matter') to two causes. One is the lack of threshold activation. The other is the training paradigm of fixed capacity on massive corpus activations. They argue that TSAE capacity must match data scale for faithful reconstruction.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates reconstruction fidelity and stability of threshold-activated and ReLU SAEs on entity-activated representations; it does not use the original dark-matter error decomposition or measure its linear predictability, tokenwise norms, or context overlap.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction results differ by SAE activation design (JumpReLU versus ReLU) and by the tested ReLU capacity; the paper also reports high TSAE reconstruction across three training-data sources.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The reconstruction experiments use subject-entity activations, and the paper does not directly test dark-matter structure or functional effects. The reported ReLU-versus-JumpReLU comparison does not isolate which training mechanism causes the fidelity difference. No uncertainty estimates are given for the reconstruction values. Some Llama3.1-8B layers were omitted after optimization failed.
record.rows_left_out: The layer-specific TSAE R2 values in Tables 4 and 5 are not separately extracted; the model-level averages are recorded in r2-r3. Table 3 q* values and Table 6 q* values measure stability rather than reconstruction fidelity. The paper's monosemanticity scores and figure-only plots are not direct measurements for V6.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input is not measured.
Per-token error-norm prediction across sizes, and whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts.
Downstream loss under spliced-in reconstructions versus random errors of the same size.
No split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.
No circuit or steering analysis with or without the error term.
Individual mechanisms (shrinkage, dead latents, L1 penalty) are not isolated. No end-to-end training. No corpus-scale token activations. No evaluation of downstream loss.

missing.what: R2 grid over TSAE capacity × data scale on Gemma2-2B, showing near-perfect reconstruction only above a capacity threshold
Per-baseline, per-layer R2 for GemmaScope 7×/28×, GemmaScope 5×/37× and LlamaScope 8×/32× (figure only)

record.verdict_notes: Reconstruction is of final-token subject-entity activations on small static datasets. Fit to a matched-capacity TSAE there is near-trivial compared with corpus-wide token activations, so generalising to dark matter in standard SAEs is uncertain. The baselines were trained on MLP outputs, and the hook site of the authors' activations is not clearly matched. No uncertainty estimates are given for R2.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of input activations.
Per-token error-norm scaling across SAE sizes, overlap in contexts where larger and smaller SAEs fail, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction replacement harms model loss more than same-size random errors.
Whether linear error contains unlearned features and nonlinear error is qualitatively distinct or resists further dictionary learning.
Whether feature-based circuit or steering analyses lose model behavior without the SAE error term.

The experiments compare reconstruction fidelity across some activation designs, capacities, and data sources, but do not establish that dark matter mostly comes from sparsity penalties, feature shrinkage, dead latents, or the objective individually; they do not test end-to-end training.

relationships.condition: JumpReLU TSAEs trained on static final-token entity activations (about 20K per layer), capacity matched to data scale, on Gemma2-2B/9B and Llama3.1-8B
relationships.reason: Error nearly vanishes (R2 about 99.9%: r1–r3, r5–r30, r44–r46). ReLU SAEs on the same Gemma2-2B layers leave 3–9% (r31–r39), so the error depends on training/activation design.

relation.reason: The study trains SAEs and measures reconstruction across activation designs, capacities, and training-data conditions.

tranche.reason: The capacity/data-scale results qualify unconditional error persistence, and the architecture comparison bears on training-sensitive reconstruction error.

source_check.notes: Appendix C.1/Table 2 supplies additional reconstruction evidence from Wikipedia and MATH500 that the pack omits. Reconstruction R2 does not establish downstream fidelity or a causal partition of dark matter; the quoted judge prompt is an experimental example.

statements.correction: Table 1: CounterFact TSAE R2 averages 99.92%, 99.93%, 99.85%. Section 4.2: corpus-trained feature comparators average 48.8% on entity activations. Downstream replacement fidelity is unmeasured. Appendix C.1 and Table 2 additionally report Wikipedia and MATH500 reconstruction ablations.
statements.problem: The numerical comparison is correct, but training-regime dependence is consistent with V6; untested downstream transfer does not establish a limits_scope verdict.

statements.correction: No quantitative partition of reconstruction error into training artifacts and representation structure is reported. The training-dynamics discussion conjectures a finite-capacity explanation and leaves theoretical characterization of corpus-trained SAEs open.
statements.problem: The missing quantitative causal partition is correctly identified, but the paper does not explicitly list that attribution as an untested part.

statements.correction: Appendix C.1/Table 2: Wikipedia R2 99.84%, MATH500 99.86%, WikiData 99.89%, with model and data scales matched. Section 4.3 uses a 1.9B-sample WikiData activation pool for the capacity/data-scale sweep. Corpus-scale arbitrary-token generalization with preserved downstream behavior remains unestablished; downstream loss is not measured.
statements.problem: The paper does not explicitly list the claimed untested items, and it includes non-entity training-source ablations omitted by this description.

statements.correction: Architecture and training comparisons establish reconstruction sensitivity. No causal partition or residual-error structure analysis is reported. The authors attribute high-fidelity reconstruction to intrinsic sparsifiability in Appendix C.6.
statements.problem: The exclusion of representation structure is unsupported, but an explicit statement leaving residual-error structure or causal attribution untested is not present.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: JumpReLU threshold-activated SAEs on the reported models and data settings
reader_labels.reason: The TSAEs attain high reconstruction fidelity in the model averages and reported Gemma2-2B layers, and high fidelity is also reported across the three training-data sources (r1-r3, r5-r30, r44-r46).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ReLU SAEs and increasing ReLU capacity at Gemma2-2B
reader_labels.reason: ReLU SAE reconstruction remains lower than the reported JumpReLU results, and the four tested capacities at layer 10 do not improve fidelity; this suggests capacity alone is insufficient, while the tested results do not isolate the specific training mechanisms named in V6 (r31-r43).
